cards.text: The prophet Zechariah is still seeing visions, and an angel is still showing him around. This time the angel shows him Joshua the high priest, standing before the angel of the LORD. And standing at Joshua's right hand? Satan.

cards.question: Satan is standing at the right hand of Joshua the high priest to ___ him.
Then the LORD speaks, and He talks straight to Satan. What does He say?

answers.text: You may test him for a time

cards.text: Then the LORD asks about Joshua: "Is not this man a firebrand snatched from the fire?" Not strolled out, not politely escorted, but SNATCHED.
Now look at Joshua, standing there before the angel. Friend, I need you to check out what this man is wearing.

cards.question: What is Joshua the high priest dressed in as he stands before the angel?
So the angel gives an order to those standing before him about Joshua. What is it?

answers.text: Send him out of the camp
Let him wash in the river

cards.question: Then the angel tells Joshua what taking off those clothes means: his ___ has been removed.
The angel also promises Joshua something new to wear: splendid robes.

cards.text: Then Zechariah himself speaks up and jumps into the vision with WARDROBE notes. I love it, because that's me every time somebody stamps a cookie crooked.

cards.question: What does Zechariah ask them to put on Joshua?

answers.text: A clean turban on his head
A signet ring on his hand

cards.text: So a clean turban goes on Joshua's head, and they clothe him, while the angel of the LORD stands by. Then the angel of the LORD gives Joshua a charge.

cards.question: The LORD's promise to Joshua starts with an "if." What does Joshua have to do?

answers.text: Walk in His ways and keep His instructions
Rebuild the wall around all of Jerusalem
Offer a lamb on the altar every morning

cards.question: If Joshua does, he'll govern the LORD's house and have charge of His courts. The LORD will also give him a place among whom?

answers.text: The ones standing there in the vision
The kings who ruled over Judah
The elders who sat at the gate

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Joshua and his companions seated before him. He says He will bring His servant, the Branch.

cards.question: The LORD tells Joshua and his companions seated before him that they are indeed what?

cards.text: Next the LORD points to a stone He has set before Joshua, with seven eyes on that one stone, and says He will engrave an inscription on it. Friend, I stamp cookies for a living, and I have NEVER stamped anything like that.

cards.question: Joshua's iniquity was removed. Now the LORD says He'll remove the iniquity of this land. How long will it take?
On that day, the LORD of Hosts says, each of them will invite a neighbor to do what?

answers.text: Sit with them under their vine and fig tree
Stand with them on guard at the city wall
Help them rebuild the house of the LORD

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave Zechariah for now. Keep your apron on, friend, because this prophet is not done seeing things yet.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 9 of the 12 choice cards are multiple choice (cards 3, 6, 7, 11, 13, 14, 16, 18, 19). There are only 2 fill in the blank cards (2, 8) and 1 true or false card (9). Cards 11 through 19 are seven multiple choice cards in a row. Several of them would work as true or false or fill in the blank, such as card 16 (sign) and card 18 (a single day).

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The opening card runs past 3 sentences: 'The prophet Zechariah is still seeing visions…', 'This time the angel shows him…', 'And standing at Joshua's right hand?', 'Satan.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card states facts from outside the passage: that Zechariah has already been seeing visions and that an angel has been showing him around. This comes from Zechariah 1–2. The card cites only Zechariah 3:1, so these facts carry no reference.

rule.text: Every fact and every verse number comes from that text. Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Verse 8 says 'you and your companions seated before you, who are indeed a sign.' The text leaves open whether 'who' means the companions alone or Joshua and the companions together. The card decides the question by saying the LORD tells Joshua and his companions that 'they' are a sign.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question says 'each of them' without saying who 'them' is. It also relies on 'On that day' from the card before, which is no longer on screen. The baker can't tell who is inviting a neighbor.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin's voice is thin across the walkthrough. Only cards 4, 10 and 17 try for a laugh, and the joke on card 4 ('Not strolled out, not politely escorted') is mild. Cards 1, 5, 12 and 15 read as plain narration with little of his voice. That includes the big moment of the Branch on card 15, and the filthy garments swapped for splendid robes, which is a natural fit for a stamper renewed from the drawer.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
